also: you can if you want to

terms.gloss: if you want to, you can
evidence: Hor. S. 2.6.39: dīxeris «experiar»: «sī vīs, potes» addit et īnstat
terms.comment: In Horace a busy acquaintance presses him to do a favour; the words themselves are the plainest Latin encouragement. To a child who says he cannot, Immō potes (“yes you can”) answers the negative.

phrases.latin: Dīxeris «experiar»: «sī vīs, potes» addit et īnstat.
phrases.english: Say “I’ll try”, and he adds, “if you want to, you can”, and keeps on at you.

phrases.latin: Hōs successus alit: possunt, quia posse videntur.
phrases.english: Success feeds them: they can because they think they can.

phrases.latin: Nōn possum, tata! — Immō potes: cōnāre modo.
phrases.english: I can’t, Dad! — Yes you can: just try.

sources: Lewis & Short: possum · Lewis & Short: immo
